relevance_reason: Case series defining the autosomal dominant FBXO31 p.Asp334Asn neurodevelopmental disorder and proposing the eponym Kruer syndrome.

findings.statement: Galaz-Montoya et al. (2026) proposed the descriptive term 'autosomal dominant FBXO31-associated neurodevelopmental disorder' and the eponym 'Kruer syndrome' for the disorder caused by the recurrent de novo FBXO31 p.Asp334Asn variant.
quotes: We propose the descriptive term "autosomal dominant FBXO31-associated neurodevelopmental disorder," and-consistent with the validating laboratory and with support from the FBXO31 Foundation-propose the eponym "Kruer syndrome."

findings.statement: Galaz-Montoya et al. (2026) reevaluated 3 previously published individuals and described 4 additional probands with the recurrent de novo FBXO31 p.Asp334Asn variant. The core phenotype comprised cerebral palsy (mixed hypotonia, spasticity, and dystonia), global developmental delay/intellectual disability, and speech impairment. Neuropsychiatric features, sometimes prominent, included ADHD, anxiety, stereotypies, autistic features, and behavioral dysregulation, and a subtle but consistent facial gestalt was noted.
quotes: we re-evaluated three published cases and ascertained four additional probands via advocacy networks, GeneMatcher, and clinician referral.
A core neurodevelopmental profile was observed and included cerebral palsy (mixed hypotonia, spasticity, and dystonia), global developmental delay/intellectual disability, and speech impairment.
Neuropsychiatric features were sometimes prominent and included attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder, anxiety, stereotypies, autistic features, and behavioral dysregulation.

findings.statement: Galaz-Montoya et al. (2026) found that neuroimaging in individuals with the FBXO31 p.Asp334Asn variant often showed a hypoplastic corpus callosum and posterior-predominant white matter changes; 1 individual also had gray matter heterotopias.
quotes: Neuroimaging often showed a hypoplastic corpus callosum and posterior-predominant white-matter changes. In one individual, gray matter heterotopias were also observed.

findings.statement: Galaz-Montoya et al. (2026) reported that all 7 individuals carried the recurrent de novo heterozygous FBXO31 c.1000G>A (p.Asp334Asn) variant, and concluded that this variant leads to a recognizable neurodevelopmental syndrome, recommending inclusion of FBXO31 in diagnostic algorithms for cerebral palsy and neurodevelopmental disorders.
quotes: All seven individuals carried the recurrent de novo FBXO31 p.Asp334Asn variant.
A recurrent de novo variant, c.1000G>A(p.Asp334Asn), has been described in association with an autosomal-dominant phenotype.
we recommend including FBXO31 in diagnostic algorithms for cerebral palsy and neurodevelopmental disorders.

findings.statement: Galaz-Montoya et al. (2026) noted that biallelic loss-of-function FBXO31 variants cause autosomal recessive intellectual disability, distinct from the autosomal dominant phenotype caused by the recurrent de novo p.Asp334Asn variant.
quotes: Biallelic loss-of-function variants in FBXO31 cause autosomal-recessive intellectual disability.

relevance_reason: This paper reports a third patient with the recurrent de novo FBXO31 p.Asp334Asn variant, which confirms the FBXO31-related spastic-dystonic cerebral palsy syndrome (Kruer syndrome).

findings.statement: Dzinovic et al. (2021) reported a 9-year-old Slovakian boy, the first child of unrelated healthy parents, who had a complex, non-progressive movement disorder dominated by spasticity and dystonia. He had hypotonia and delayed development in infancy. He spoke single words at 12 months but lost speech at 18 months. By age 2 years his hypotonia had converted to limb spasticity, worse in the legs, and he had dystonic posturing of all four limbs. A working diagnosis of spastic-dystonic cerebral palsy was made. At age 9 years he had generalized dystonia, spasticity, hyperreflexia, leg clonus, an unsteady spastic-dystonic gait, no expressive language and moderate intellectual disability, without dysmorphic features. Brain MRI at age 3 years showed reduced parietal and occipital white matter volume and global white matter dysmyelination.
quotes: We report the case of a 9‐year‐old boy demonstrating a complex, non‐progressive movement‐disorder syndrome dominated by spasticity and dystonia (Table 1).
Neuropediatric assessment at the age of 2 years documented a conversion to limb spasticity from hypotonia, more pronounced in the lower extremities.
On brain MRI (age 3 years), there was reduced white‐matter volume in the parietal and occipital lobes bilaterally, along with an aspect of global white‐matter dysmyelination.

phenotypes.text: limb spasticity, lower more than upper

findings.statement: Trio whole-exome sequencing by Dzinovic et al. (2021) found that the proband was heterozygous for a de novo c.1000G>A (p.Asp334Asn) missense variant in FBXO31. This is the same variant previously reported in 2 unrelated patients with spastic diplegic cerebral palsy. The variant was absent from gnomAD and in-house exomes. It affects a conserved residue in the domain that interacts with the substrate cyclin D1, and it was classified as pathogenic. No other potentially disease-relevant variants were found.
quotes: The analysis revealed that the proband was heterozygous for a FBXO31 c.1000G > A (p. Asp334Asn) missense substitution, which had occurred de novo.
This variant, absent from control databases (gnomAD, in‐house exomes), has been described recently in two individuals with an NDD diagnosed as spastic diplegic CP.
The variant affected a conserved residue within a functionally important domain of the encoded protein, involved in the interaction with FBXO31`s substrate cyclin‐D1 (Fig. 1A and B).

findings.statement: Dzinovic et al. (2021) compared their patient with the 2 patients previously reported with the same variant. All 3 had motor and/or speech delay, mild to moderate intellectual disability, neonatal hypotonia and lower-limb-predominant spasticity, and each had been diagnosed with cerebral palsy. Dystonia was present only in their patient. The following were each found in 1 or 2 of the 3 patients: congenital malformations (cleft palate and intestinal malrotation in 1), ADHD (2), strabismus or esotropia (2), and brain MRI abnormalities.
quotes: The three cases shared a presentation of motor and/or speech delay, and all had ID that varied from mild to moderate.

The latter comprised spasticity (as seen in all three patients), predominantly affecting the lower limbs and leading to a diagnosis of CP in each subject, as well as dystonia (observed in the herein reported case).

Other neurological and non‐neurological manifestations such as congenital malformations, behavioral issues, minor dysmorphia, and neuroanatomical alterations occurred in two or only one of the subjects.

findings.statement: Dzinovic et al. (2021) suggested that the emerging hallmarks of FBXO31-related disease were delayed psychomotor development, dysfunction of both the pyramidal and extrapyramidal systems (spasticity and dystonia), impaired expressive and receptive language, and intellectual disability. They concluded that a recurrent de novo missense variant in FBXO31 causes an autosomal dominant neurodevelopmental syndrome with prominent motor dysfunction.
quotes: Emerging hallmarks of FBXO31‐related disease seem to include a delay in psychomotor development, dysfunction of both pyramidal and extrapyramidal systems (as evidenced by the manifestation of spasticity and dystonia), impairments in expressive and receptive language, and ID.
Our data confirm a link between variant FBXO31 and an autosomal dominant neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by prominent motor dysfunction.

relevance_reason: Reports two unrelated patients with spastic diplegic cerebral palsy, intellectual disability and other features who carried an identical de novo FBXO31 p.Asp334Asn variant. Functional work in patient fibroblasts showed reduced cyclin D, which defines the Kruer syndrome phenotype.

findings.statement: Jin et al. (2020) described 2 unrelated patients (F218 and F699) from a cohort of 250 cerebral palsy trios. Both had spastic diplegic cerebral palsy, intellectual disability, expressive language disorder and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder. Patient F218 also had gut malrotation, constipation, cleft palate and strabismus, and brain MRI was normal. Patient F699 had strabismus, severe constipation, and ventricular dilation with a thin corpus callosum on MRI.
quotes: Both patients in our cohort exhibited spastic diplegic CP (Supplementary Table 4 and Supplementary Videos F218 and F699), ID, expressive language disorder and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder.

F218 had gut malrotation and constipation, cleft palate, strabismus and normal brain morphology on MRI, while F699 had strabismus, severe constipation and ventricular dilation with thin corpus callosum on MRI.

findings.statement: Jin et al. (2020) performed whole-exome sequencing of 250 cerebral palsy parent-offspring trios and found the same de novo heterozygous missense variant in FBXO31, p.Asp334Asn (D334N), in 2 unrelated patients. Sanger sequencing of the mothers, fathers and probands confirmed de novo inheritance. Asp334 is a conserved residue in the FBXO31 binding pocket that is thought to mediate hydrogen bonding to cyclin D1, and structural modeling predicted that the variant changes the surface electrostatic charge around the cyclin D1-binding site.
quotes: We also identified two unrelated cases with an identical DNM (encoding p.Asp334Asn; Fig. 2a and Supplementary Table 4) in FBXO31, which encodes the F-box only protein 31.
Asp334 is a conserved residue within the binding pocket on FBXO31 (Fig. 2b), where it is thought to mediate hydrogen bonding to cyclin D1 (ref.).
a, Sanger traces of the mother, father and proband from families F218 and F699 verify de novo inheritance and the position of the variant (red arrow).

findings.statement: Jin et al. (2020) found that fibroblasts from both patients carrying FBXO31 p.Asp334Asn had less cyclin D than control fibroblasts (P = 0.004). The authors concluded that the variant affects the cyclin D interaction site and causes an apparent gain of function in cyclin D degradation.
quotes: FBXO31 p.Asp334Asn affects the cyclin D interaction site (Fig. 2b), leading to an apparent gain of function of cyclin D degradation (Fig. 2c).
both patients had reduced cyclin D compared to pooled controls. the data are averaged for three independent cell culture experiments (n = 7 controls, n = 6 patient measurements).

findings.statement: Jin et al. (2020) concluded that the de novo FBXO31 p.Asp334Asn variant causes a phenotype distinct from the nonsyndromic intellectual disability previously reported with an autosomal recessive homozygous truncating FBXO31 mutation. They suggested that their findings likely represent a phenotypic expansion.
quotes: Therefore, this DNM in FBXO31 leads to a phenotype distinct from the previously described autosomal recessive truncating mutation-associated non-syndromic ID phenotype.
In other cases, typified by FBXO31, our findings likely represent phenotypic expansions.
